interview.title: Mock interview
interview.subtitle: One or two problems, a clock, and no way to look up the answer. Then a debrief.

formatBlurb.warmUp: A single question, the length of a quick screen. Good for shaking off the rust.
formatBlurb.standard: The one to practise. An easier opener, then the real question — the shape of most technical screens.
formatBlurb.hard: The same shape pitched higher: a medium to open, then a hard one. For the round after the screen.

interview.resumeTitle: You have a round in progress
interview.rulesClock: The clock runs on the server. Closing the tab does not pause it, and the round ends when it reaches zero.
interview.rulesSequence: One problem at a time. The next opens when you solve the current one, or decide to move on from it — and moving on is final.
interview.rulesEditorial: Editorials and topic tags stay hidden until the round is over. Afterwards every problem links straight to its write-up.
interview.rulesHints: Hints are there if you need them, and each one is noted in the debrief. Nothing is deducted — it just gets said.
interview.rulesUnseen: Problems you have never attempted come up first, and anything from your last two weeks of interviews is skipped.
interview.rulesPrivate: Your results are yours. Nothing here is shared, ranked or compared with anybody else.
interview.noHistoryBody: Sit one and the debrief will show up here.

outcomeBlurb.noSolve: Nothing went in this time. Read both editorials, then sit the same format again in a day or two.
outcomeBlurb.partial: Some of it went in. The one you did not get is the one worth reading up on.
outcomeBlurb.solid: You got through the set — with a hint, or with the clock closing in. Both are fine in a real round.
outcomeBlurb.strong: Everything solved, unaided, with time to spare. That is the round you want to have.

interview.finishBody: The round ends now and you go to the debrief. Anything unsolved stays unsolved.
interview.finishBodySolved: You have solved everything. Finishing now records the time you did it in.
interview.abandonBody: The round is thrown away rather than scored. It stays in your history as abandoned.
interview.hintCost: Revealing a hint is noted in the debrief. It costs you no points.
interview.editorialLocked: The editorial and the topic tags are locked until the round is over.
interview.abandonedBody: You walked out of this one, so it has no result. That is not the same as failing it.
interview.stillRunningBody: This round has not finished yet. Go back to it, or finish it to get a result.
interview.usedOutsideHelp: I looked something up during this round
interview.usedOutsideHelpHint: Nothing changes if you tick this. It is here so the numbers above are still worth reading later.

insight.noSubmission: Nothing was submitted. Even a brute force beats an empty editor — in a real round it is what the conversation is built on.
insight.allSolved: You solved the whole set inside the time.
insight.cleanRun: Everything solved, one submission each, no hints. That is as clean as a round gets.
insight.finishedEarly: You finished with a good part of the clock unspent — room a real interviewer would fill with follow-ups.
insight.ranOutOfTime: The clock ran out with problems still open. Watch for the point where a working brute force beats an unfinished optimal one.
insight.slowWarmUp: The warm-up took most of the round. It is meant to be the cheap one, and banking it quickly is what buys time for the hard question.
insight.hintsUsed: You took a hint. Worth re-reading that problem's editorial to see what it was pointing at.
insight.manyAttempts: Several submissions per solve. Reading your own code once before submitting is faster than the judge is.
insight.skippedProblem: You moved on from a problem. Good instinct if it was deliberate — a real round rewards it.

interview.skipBody: You will not be able to come back to it. That is the point: knowing when to cut your losses is half of what a two-problem round tests.
interview.problemClosed: You have moved on from this problem. It stays here to read, but it can no longer be edited or submitted.
interview.showingSubmitted: This is the code you submitted, exactly as it was judged. The problem is closed, so it can no longer be edited.
interview.lockedHint: Solve or move on from the current problem to open this one.

form.basicsHelp: What the problem is called, where it lives, and who can see it.
form.title: Title
form.slugLock: Stop the slug following the title
form.slugUnlock: Let the slug follow the title again
form.stateHelpDraft: Invisible to solvers. Only you can open it.
form.stateHelpArchived: Out of the catalogue; past submissions still resolve.
form.publishBlocked: This problem cannot be published yet:
form.statementHelp: Markdown. This is the problem as a solver reads it.
form.constraintsHelp: Keep these honest about the hidden cases a submission is judged against.
form.examplesHelp: The worked examples printed in the statement. Prose, not data — the judge never reads these.
form.noExamples: No examples yet. A published problem needs at least one.
form.explanationHelp: Optional. Why that input gives that output.
form.hintsHelp: Revealed one at a time, in this order. The first should nudge; the last may give the approach away.
form.signatureHelp: The function a solver implements. It drives the starter code, the harness that reads stdin, and how a return value is printed — so the test cases below are written against it.
form.noSignature: Without a signature this problem has no editor to solve it in, and cannot be published.
form.functionNameHelp: As it appears in every language, e.g. twoSum
form.noParameters: No arguments. A test case's input will be empty.
form.testCasesHelp: Samples are shown to the solver and are what “Run” judges. Hidden cases are the bar a submission has to clear.
form.testCasesNoSignature: Declare a signature above and each case will be checked for the right number of input lines.
form.inputShape_other: {{count}} lines per case, in this order: {{names}}
form.verifyHelp: Runs a correct solution against every stored case, hidden ones included. Nothing is recorded and no submission is made.
form.verifyUnsaved: Save the problem first — this runs against the stored test cases.
form.verifyDirty: There are unsaved changes. This runs against the last saved test cases.
form.verifyPassed: Every case matches its expected output.
form.editorialHelp: The written solution: the approach, why the obvious attempt falls short, and code that works.
form.noEditorial: No editorial. The reader's tab stays disabled.

contest.rejudgeConfirmBody: Fix the problem in the catalogue first. This freezes the corrected version onto the contest and re-judges everything against it.

contest.rulesFrozen: The problems are frozen when the contest starts, so everybody is judged on the same tests.
